     3	/-!
     4	# Expanded line measurements
     5	
     6	For a generalized-Pauli basis `W` and a canonical line, the expanded line
     7	measurement is the convolution of the strategy line measurement with the
     8	projective measurement of one Pauli register whose outcome is the restriction
     9	to that line of the low-degree encoding of the measured basis label. This file
    10	states the three consistency conclusions the source draws for that family,
    11	together with the existential form in which the source states them.
    12	
    13	The argument runs as follows. Restricting a multilinear low-degree encoding to
    14	a line gives a polynomial of degree at most `m*d` in the line parameter, and at
    15	most `d` on an axis-parallel line (`LineMeasurement.Restriction`), whose
    16	partial evaluation at a sampled point obeys the elementary calculus of
    17	`LineMeasurement.Evaluation`.
    18	Coarse-graining the generalized Pauli basis measurement along that restriction
    19	gives the ancillary projectors `tau^{W,line}`, which are symmetric and hence
    20	perfectly self-consistent on an EPR pair (`LineMeasurement.Projector`). Their
    21	convolution with the strategy line measurement is again projective and vanishes
    22	outside the degree-`d` outcomes on an axis line (`LineMeasurement.Expanded`).
    23	Self-consistency of the convolution follows from self-consistency of the
    24	strategy line measurements and the data-processing inequality
    25	(`LineMeasurement.SelfConsistency`). The overlap of an expanded line
    26	measurement with the expanded point effects selected by evaluation at the
    27	sampled point factorizes exactly through the ancillary consistency of
    28	`tau^{W,line}` with `tau^{W,u}` (`LineMeasurement.LinePointOverlap`); the
    29	generic bipartite estimates of `LineMeasurement.BipartiteTransport` carry that
    30	overlap to the two bipartitions of the six registers, giving the
    31	evaluation-class conclusion (`LineMeasurement.EvalClassConsistency`) and, by
    32	projective refinement, the line-versus-point conclusion
    33	(`LineMeasurement.LinePointConsistency`).
    34	
    35	Two features of this route differ from the source. The source derives its third
    36	item from its second; here the evaluation-class estimate comes first, from the
    37	exact overlap identity, and the second item follows from it by projective
    38	refinement, so that the source's elementary sub-measurement inequality is not
    39	needed. The source also transports a relation proved for one pair of register
    40	placements to the remaining three by the symmetry of the test
    41	(`lem:symmetric-equivalents-transfer`, which is not formalized); here each of
    42	the four directed opposite-placement pairs is proved directly. The estimates
    43	established are linear in `ε` for all three items, hence stronger than the
    44	square-root error whenever `ε ≤ 1`; they are weakened to the common error
    45	`deltaLine ε = √ε` only because the source states the three items with a single
    46	error function (`LineMeasurement.SquareRootError`).
    47

    50	The declarations formalize `def:expanded-line-measurement` and

    52	Their paper source is
    53	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:523-678`.
    54	-/

 	$f,g\in K^{c+1}$ be distinct coefficient vectors. Their polynomials
 	$p_f(T)=\sum_{i=0}^{c}f_iT^i$ and $p_g(T)=\sum_{i=0}^{c}g_iT^i$

 \begin{definition}[The concrete paired-line POVM]
 	\label{def:concrete-paired-line-measurement}
 	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.ProjectiveSetting.combinedLineMeasurement}
 	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.ProjectiveSetting.combinedLineMeasurement_effect}
 	\leanok
 	\uses{def:expanded-line-measurement, def:povm-conventions,
 		def:ideg-deg-polynomials}
 	For any projective setting, either player, and any two source lines,
 	define the POVM on the expanded local space by
 	\[
 		T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}
 		=\hat M^{(\mathrm{Line},X),\ell_X}_{f_X}
 		 \hat M^{(\mathrm{Line},Z),\ell_Z}_{f_Z}
 		 \hat M^{(\mathrm{Line},X),\ell_X}_{f_X},
 		\qquad (f_X,f_Z)\in\deg_{md}(\ell_X)\times\deg_{md}(\ell_Z).
 	\]
 	Each effect is positive. Summing first over $f_Z$ and then over $f_X$
 	gives the identity by completeness and projectivity of the line
 	measurements. This is the construction in the proof of
 	Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-xz-lines} in \cite{Ji2020MIPStar}.
 \end{definition}

 \section{Applying the classical low-degree test}
 \label{sec:apply-ldt}
 
 The combined point and line measurements of the previous two sections are next
 merged into a single measurement returning a pair of global polynomials that
 encode the $X$-basis and the $Z$-basis information simultaneously. This is
 done by encoding the pair as one polynomial in $2m+2$ variables and invoking
 the quantum soundness of the classical low individual degree test
 (Theorem~\ref{lem:ld-soundness}). The classical game, its question
 distribution, and the line-point distribution are defined at dimension $2m+2$
 only when $2m+2$ divides $q$ (Definition~\ref{def:ld-game}), a condition that
 admissibility of $(q,m,d)$ does not supply; the statements below are the
 source statements, without that condition, and their proofs are blocked at
 the instantiation step for admissible parameters with $m \ge 2$. The
 obstruction is recorded in Remark~\ref{rem:qld-4-7-divisibility} and
 analyzed, together with candidate repairs, in
 \cite{gap:qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility}.
 
 \begin{definition}[The combining map]

 	For $f, g \in \mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\F_q)$, the polynomial
 	$\mathrm{combine}_{f,g} \in \mathrm{ideg}_{d,2m+2}(\F_q)$ is defined by
 	\[
 		\mathrm{combine}_{f,g}(x, z, \alpha, \beta)
 		= \alpha f(x) + \beta g(z)\,,
 		\qquad x \in \F_q^m,\ z \in \F_q^m,\ \alpha \in \F_q,\
 		\beta \in \F_q\,.
 	\]
 	The combining map is also defined for polynomials restricted to lines.
 	Let $\ell$ be a line in $\F_q^{2m+2}$ with intercept
 	$u = (u_X, u_Z, u_\alpha, u_\beta)$ and slope
 	$v = (v_X, v_Z, v_\alpha, v_\beta)$, and let $\ell_X$ and $\ell_Z$ be
 	lines in $\F_q^m$ such that for every point
 	$(x, z, \alpha, \beta) \in \ell$ it holds that $x \in \ell_X$ and
 	$z \in \ell_Z$. Then for any two polynomials
 	$f \in \deg_{md}(\ell_X)$ and $g \in \deg_{md}(\ell_Z)$, the polynomial
 	$\mathrm{combine}_{f,g} \in \deg_{md+1}(\ell)$ is defined by
 	\begin{equation}
 		\label{eq:combine-lines}
 		\mathrm{combine}_{f,g}(u + t \cdot v)
 		= (u_\alpha + t \cdot v_\alpha)\, f(u_X + t \cdot v_X)
 		+ (u_\beta + t \cdot v_\beta)\, g(u_Z + t \cdot v_Z)\,,
 		\qquad t \in \F_q\,.
 	\end{equation}
 	The degree bound holds because $f$ and $g$, restricted to lines, are
 	polynomials of degree at most $md$ in the line parameter, and each is
 	multiplied by an affine factor of degree at most one.
 \end{definition}

 \section{The domain of the conditional Lean helper}
 
 The source statement does not take an arbitrary joint point measurement as an
 input.  It uses the family $\{\hat Q^{x,z}_{a,b}\}$ constructed by the preceding
 point lemma, whose error has the form $\delta_Q(\eps)=\poly(\eps)$.  Consequently,
 an internal theorem which accepts an already constructed point witness must retain
 the same quantitative dependency: it should first fix a function
 $\delta_Q:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ satisfying the one-variable polynomial-error
 predicate, then choose $\delta_P$, and at strategy error $\eps$ accept only a
 point witness with bound $\delta_Q(\eps)$.
 
 Before the repair tracked by \ghissue{389}, the Lean helper
 \path{exists_combinedLinesWitness_ofPointsWitness} instead had the quantifier
 order
 \[
   \exists\delta_P=\poly(\eps,md/q)\quad
   \forall\eps\ \forall\delta_Q\ \forall Q,
   \qquad Q\text{ has point error at most }\delta_Q
   \Longrightarrow T\text{ has line error at most }\delta_P(\eps,md/q).
 \]
 Thus the line-error function was chosen before an unrestricted scalar
 $\delta_Q$, and did not depend on it.  The fields of
 \path{CombinedPointsWitness} bound self-consistency and the two ordered-product
 comparisons by precisely this scalar; they impose no relation between an
 arbitrary $\delta_Q$ and $\eps$.  The conditioned-pasting estimate therefore
 cannot eliminate $\delta_Q$ from its conclusion.
 
 There is a concrete mathematical obstruction to the old domain.  Set
 $\eps=0$, take $m=1$ and fixed $d$, and let $q$ grow through admissible field
 sizes with $q>d+1$.  On any perfect strategy, define the supplied projective
 joint point measurement deterministically, with X answer $x^{d+1}$ and a fixed
 Z answer, identically on the two player sides.  Its self-consistency defect is
 zero, while the two ordered-product defects are finite and hence can be covered
 by a sufficiently large scalar $\delta_Q$, which the old helper quantified
 arbitrarily.  On an axis X line, however, every outcome allowed by
 \path{CombinedLinesWitness.axis_degree_X} evaluates as a polynomial of degree at
 most $d$.  Its difference from $x^{d+1}$ has at most $d+1$ roots, so even after
 mixing line outcomes the disagreement probability on that line is at least
 $1-(d+1)/q$.  Since axis lines have fixed positive weight in the line-point
 law, the resulting line consistency defect stays bounded away from zero as
 $q\to\infty$.  In contrast, the two-variable polynomial-error predicate forces
 $\delta_P(0,d/q)\to0$.  This argument diagnoses the theorem interface; no Lean
 counterexample theorem is asserted here.
 
 The repaired conditional helper has the form
 \[
   \forall\delta_Q,\quad \delta_Q=\poly(\eps)\Longrightarrow
   \exists\delta_P=\poly(\eps,md/q)\quad
   \forall\eps\ \forall Q\text{ with error }\delta_Q(\eps),\quad
   \exists T\text{ with error }\delta_P(\eps,md/q).
 \]
 This is not a new hypothesis on the paper theorem.  The source-facing Lean
 declaration \path{exists_combinedLinesWitness} preserves its original statement:
 it existentially obtains $\delta_Q$ and its point witnesses from the preceding
 point construction, then applies the conditional helper.

 The same quantitative omission remains in the auxiliary
 \path{exists_extendedLinesWitness_ofPointsWitness}: a single polynomial error
 function is chosen before an arbitrary scalar $\delta_Q$ and every point witness
 at that error. Passing from paired points to the extended scalar answer does

 problem: it still tends to zero at $\eps=0$ with fixed $m,d$ and increasing $q$.
 These unrestricted auxiliaries are tracked by \ghissue{509} and \ghissue{511},
 respectively. The source instead uses the family constructed by its point lemma,
 with $\delta_Q=\poly(\eps)$, and defines the scalar answer by
 $c=\alpha a+\beta b$. Claim~17-1 explicitly retains the point error.
 \footnote{The source passages are \path{lem:qld-4-10}, \path{lem:qld-4-12}, and
 \path{claim:17-1} in
 \path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex},
 lines~689--709, 993--1018, and 1140--1173.}
 
 Take $m=d=1$, $\eps=0$, and let $q=2^{2k+1}>2$ tend to infinity.
 These parameters are admissible. The Pauli basis test has a perfect projective strategy by
 \path{lem:pauli-completeness}.\footnote{See
 \path{references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex},
 lines~1229--1421, for the construction; the statement and its projective Pauli
 measurements appear at lines~1232--1255.}
 Let $\hat\psi$ be its normalized expanded state. On each player's expanded
 local space, define the supplied joint point measurement by
 \[
  Q^{x,z}_{a,b}=
  \begin{cases}
    \Id,&(a,b)=(x^2,0),\\
    0,&\text{otherwise}.
  \end{cases}
 \]
 This is a complete projective measurement and is exactly self-consistent in
 every opposite placement. The finitely many averaged squared distances from the
 two ordered expanded point products are finite real numbers. Taking their
 maximum and zero gives a scalar $\delta_Q$ satisfying all the fields of the
 point witness. No estimate of this scalar in terms of $\eps$ is required.
 
 The extended point answer is $\alpha x^2$. In dimension $2m+2=4$, the directly
 indexed line-point law assigns weight $1/2$ to axis lines and then chooses one
 of the four coordinates uniformly. Its X-axis branch therefore has mass $1/8$.
 On that branch, $z,\alpha,\beta$ are fixed along the line, while $x$ is uniform
 in the field. The canonical base has X coordinate zero, so the affine line
 parameter is exactly $x$. For $\alpha\ne0$, every permitted line answer $p$
 has degree at most one, and $p(X)-\alpha X^2$ is a nonzero polynomial of degree
 two. It has at most two roots, hence its agreement with the point answer is at
 most $2/q$.
 
 This bound also holds for any line POVM. Indeed, for a fixed line let $w_p$
 be the expectation of its effect for $p$ in the expanded state, at the line
 player's placement. Positivity and completeness give $w_p\ge0$ and
 $\sum_p w_p=1$; the axis-degree field makes $w_p=0$ for higher-degree answers.
 The opposite point effect is deterministically the identity at $\alpha x^2$,
 so the agreement is precisely the $w_p$-weighted average of those root-count
 fractions. These weights depend on the line but not on $x$ along it. Averaging
 over the fixed coordinates, and using nonnegativity of the defect on the
 remaining question branches, gives for either player orientation
 \[
  \operatorname{defect}\ \ge\
  \frac18\left(1-\frac1q\right)\left(1-\frac2q\right).
 \]
 There is no undefined evaluation on these nonzero axis directions, so the
 completed answer alphabet does not change this calculation. The scalar field
 identification preserves the polynomial evaluations and their root counts.
 
 The lower bound tends to $1/8$. In contrast, the predicate
 \path{IsPolyErr}\textsubscript{2} bounds the proposed error at these parameters by
 $\delta_{\mathrm{combine}}(0,1/q)\le Cq^{-s}$ with $s>0$, which tends to zero.
 For the first-route estimate, the polynomial-error bound on $g$ likewise gives
 fixed constants $K\ge1$ and $r,s>0$ with
 $C g(0,1/q)\le CKq^{-s}\longrightarrow0$.
 Consequently both unrestricted supplied-point auxiliaries are false,
 independently of the printed-error discrepancy and the diagonal-line degeneracy.
 This argument does not refute the existential point-witness declarations or the source
 \path{lem:qld-4-13}; neither requires a line approximation to every arbitrarily
 chosen point family.

   120	\section{The domain of the conditional Lean helper}

   123	input.  It uses the family $\{\hat Q^{x,z}_{a,b}\}$ constructed by the preceding
   124	point lemma, whose error has the form $\delta_Q(\eps)=\poly(\eps)$.  Consequently,
   125	an internal theorem which accepts an already constructed point witness must retain
   126	the same quantitative dependency: it should first fix a function
   127	$\delta_Q:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ satisfying the one-variable polynomial-error
   128	predicate, then choose $\delta_P$, and at strategy error $\eps$ accept only a
   129	point witness with bound $\delta_Q(\eps)$.

   131	Before the repair tracked by \ghissue{389}, the Lean helper
   132	\path{exists_combinedLinesWitness_ofPointsWitness} instead had the quantifier
   133	order

   135	  \exists\delta_P=\poly(\eps,md/q)\quad
   136	  \forall\eps\ \forall\delta_Q\ \forall Q,
   137	  \qquad Q\text{ has point error at most }\delta_Q
   138	  \Longrightarrow T\text{ has line error at most }\delta_P(\eps,md/q).
   139	\]
   140	Thus the line-error function was chosen before an unrestricted scalar
   141	$\delta_Q$, and did not depend on it.  The fields of
   142	\path{CombinedPointsWitness} bound self-consistency and the two ordered-product
   143	comparisons by precisely this scalar; they impose no relation between an
   144	arbitrary $\delta_Q$ and $\eps$.  The conditioned-pasting estimate therefore
   145	cannot eliminate $\delta_Q$ from its conclusion.
   146	
   147	There is a concrete mathematical obstruction to the old domain.  Set
   148	$\eps=0$, take $m=1$ and fixed $d$, and let $q$ grow through admissible field
   149	sizes with $q>d+1$.  On any perfect strategy, define the supplied projective
   150	joint point measurement deterministically, with X answer $x^{d+1}$ and a fixed
   151	Z answer, identically on the two player sides.  Its self-consistency defect is
   152	zero, while the two ordered-product defects are finite and hence can be covered
   153	by a sufficiently large scalar $\delta_Q$, which the old helper quantified
   154	arbitrarily.  On an axis X line, however, every outcome allowed by
   155	\path{CombinedLinesWitness.axis_degree_X} evaluates as a polynomial of degree at
   156	most $d$.  Its difference from $x^{d+1}$ has at most $d+1$ roots, so even after

   161	$\delta_P(0,d/q)\to0$.  This argument diagnoses the theorem interface; no Lean

   167	  \exists\delta_P=\poly(\eps,md/q)\quad
   168	  \forall\eps\ \forall Q\text{ with error }\delta_Q(\eps),\quad

    86	\section{A counterexample to the enlarged domain}
    87	
    88	Choose an admissible tuple with $q>1$ and a perfect projective strategy.
    89	The honest strategy in the completeness lemma supplies one; for example,
    90	$(q,m,d)=(8,1,1)$ is admissible. Its expanded state has norm one. For
    91	$a\in\F_q$, let $c_a$ be the constant polynomial with value $a$. For both
    92	players and every line pair, define a POVM by
    93	\[
    94	 T_{c_a,c_b}=q^{-2}I\quad(a,b\in\F_q),\qquad
    95	 T_{f_X,f_Z}=0\quad\text{for every other pair}.
    96	\]
    97	There are $q^2$ nonzero effects, so they sum to $I$. Both axis-degree
    98	requirements hold. At any incident point a constant polynomial has a
    99	uniquely determined value, even on a zero-direction line. Thus the optional
   100	evaluation in Lean returns the ordinary field value, never an undefined
   101	outcome, for every nonzero effect in this example.
   102	
   103	The evaluated POVM is uniform on the $q^2$ point pairs. Against any complete
   104	joint point measurement $Q$, its agreement is $q^{-2}$ and its consistency
   105	defect is $1-q^{-2}$. Therefore the line-witness requirements hold with
   106	$\delta_P=1$ in every opposite placement. A point witness also exists within
   107	the former public domain: take the projective measurement which always
   108	answers $(0,0)$. It is exactly self-consistent and has both ordered-product
   109	distances at most $4$. Indeed, the squared norms of either ordered product
   110	family sum to one, by projectivity and completeness, and
   111	\begin{align*}
   112	 \sum_{a,b}\|(Q_{a,b}-M^X_aM^Z_b)\widehat\psi\|^2
   113	 &\leq 2\sum_{a,b}\|Q_{a,b}\widehat\psi\|^2\\
   114	 &\quad+2\sum_{a,b}\|M^X_aM^Z_b\widehat\psi\|^2\\
   115	 &=4.
   116	\end{align*}
   117	The reversed ordering satisfies the same calculation. Hence $\delta_Q=4$
   118	is allowed by every point-witness field. These constants are permitted by
   119	the former scalar quantifiers; the argument does not require them to be
   120	polynomially small functions of $\eps$.
   121	
   122	For each supported subline sample, completeness gives
   123	\[
   124	 A(T)=q^{-2}\sum_{a,b}\langle\widehat\psi,
   125	    (I\ot M^Z_bM^X_a)\widehat\psi\rangle=q^{-2},
   126	 \qquad
   127	 B(T)=q^{-2}\sum_{a,b}\langle\widehat\psi,
   128	    (I\ot M^Z_b)\widehat\psi\rangle=q^{-1}.
   129	\]
   130	The first equality uses $\sum_bM^Z_b\sum_aM^X_a=I$, without a commutation
   131	assumption. Probability averaging preserves these constants. The absolute
   132	difference is therefore $(q-1)/q^2>0$, whereas the claimed bound is zero at
   133	$\eps=0$. For $q=8$ the difference is $7/64$. The same perfect strategy is
   134	admissible at arbitrarily small positive $\eps$, so excluding zero or
   135	enlarging a universal constant cannot repair the claim. No polynomially
   136	vanishing error depending on $\eps$ alone absorbs this difference.

     5	# Placement calculus on the expanded state
     6	
     7	This module records the algebra of the four register placements used by the
     8	combining argument: a placement is a unital `*`-homomorphism, placements on
     9	opposite register pairs commute, and the crosswise exchange of the two EPR
    10	pairs of the expanded state carries the placement `AA'` to `AB''` and `BA''`
    11	to `BB'` while fixing the expanded state.  The last fact transfers every
    12	state-dependent distance between the two bipartition schemes of
    13	`def:symmetric-equivalents` without assuming a symmetric strategy.
    14	
    15	## References
    16	
    17	The placements are those of `def:symmetric-equivalents`, blueprint
    18	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch14_qpbt_observables.tex`, paper
    19	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:420-450`.
    20	The EPR-exchange invariance is proved directly for the involution
    21	`(A' B'')(A'' B')`, which fixes the strategy registers.  Its use for
    22	`lem:qld-4-10` is explained in `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_combined-points-direct.tex`.
    23	-/

    38	/-! ## The crosswise exchange of the two EPR pairs -/
    39	
    40	/-- The permutation of the six registers exchanging `A'` with `B''` and `A''`
    41	with `B'`, while fixing `A` and `B`.  This involution exchanges the two EPR
    42	pairs and reverses the order within each pair. -/
    43	def eprCrossSwap (P : AdmissibleParams) (ιA ιB : Type*) :
    44	    SixReg P ιA ιB ≃ SixReg P ιA ιB where
    45	  toFun := fun ⟨⟨a, a', a''⟩, b, b', b''⟩ => ((a, (b'', b')), (b, (a'', a')))
    46	  invFun := fun ⟨⟨a, a', a''⟩, b, b', b''⟩ => ((a, (b'', b')), (b, (a'', a')))
    47	  left_inv := by rintro ⟨⟨a, a', a''⟩, b, b', b''⟩; rfl
    48	  right_inv := by rintro ⟨⟨a, a', a''⟩, b, b', b''⟩; rfl
    49	
    50	/-- The EPR vector is symmetric in its two registers. -/
    51	theorem eprState_ofLp_swap {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    52	    [Nonempty V] (x y : V) :
    53	    (eprState V).ofLp (x, y) = (eprState V).ofLp (y, x) := by
    54	  change (if x = y then (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card V : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹ else 0) =
    55	    (if y = x then (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card V : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹ else 0)
    56	  by_cases h : x = y
    57	  · simp [h]
    58	  · simp [h, Ne.symm h]
    59	
    60	/-- The crosswise EPR exchange fixes the expanded state: the two EPR factors
    61	are identical and each is symmetric under exchange of its registers.  No
    62	symmetry of the strategy state is required. -/
    63	theorem reindexState_eprCrossSwap_psiHat (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) :
    64	    reindexState (eprCrossSwap P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) S.psiHat =
    65	      S.psiHat := by
    66	  ext i
    67	  obtain ⟨⟨a, a', a''⟩, b, b', b''⟩ := i
    68	  change S.toStrategy.ψ.ofLp (a, b) * (eprState (PauliRegister P)).ofLp (b'', b') *
    69	      (eprState (PauliRegister P)).ofLp (a'', a') =
    70	    S.toStrategy.ψ.ofLp (a, b) * (eprState (PauliRegister P)).ofLp (a', a'') *
    71	      (eprState (PauliRegister P)).ofLp (b', b'')
    72	  rw [eprState_ofLp_swap b'' b', eprState_ofLp_swap a'' a']
    73	  ring
    74	
    75	/-- The crosswise EPR exchange carries the `AB''` placement to the `AA'`
    76	placement. -/
    77	theorem reindexOp_eprCrossSwap_place_AB'' (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
    78	    (O : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace .alice)) :
    79	    reindexOp (eprCrossSwap P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
    80	      (S.place .AB'' O) = S.place .AA' O := by
    81	  ext i j
    82	  obtain ⟨⟨a, a', a''⟩, b, b', b''⟩ := i
    83	  obtain ⟨⟨c, c', c''⟩, d, d', d''⟩ := j
    84	  simp only [reindexOp, Matrix.reindex_apply, Matrix.submatrix_apply,
    85	    Equiv.symm_symm, place, eprCrossSwap, Equiv.coe_fn_mk, Matrix.one_apply]
    86	  ring!

    89	placement. -/
    90	theorem reindexOp_eprCrossSwap_place_BB' (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)

    92	    reindexOp (eprCrossSwap P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
    93	      (S.place .BB' O) = S.place .BA'' O := by

    96	  obtain ⟨⟨c, c', c''⟩, d, d', d''⟩ := j
    97	  simp only [reindexOp, Matrix.reindex_apply, Matrix.submatrix_apply,
    98	    Equiv.symm_symm, place, eprCrossSwap, Equiv.coe_fn_mk, Matrix.one_apply]
    99	  ring!

   101	/-- An operator placed on `AB''` has, on the expanded state, the same norm as
   102	the same operator placed on `AA'`, by invariance under the crosswise EPR
   103	exchange. -/
   104	theorem norm_place_AB''_eq_norm_place_AA' (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   105	    (O : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace .alice)) :
   106	    ‖applyOperatorToState (S.place .AB'' O) S.psiHat‖ =
   107	      ‖applyOperatorToState (S.place .AA' O) S.psiHat‖ := by
   108	  conv_lhs => rw [← reindexState_eprCrossSwap_psiHat S]
   109	  rw [WinImplications.norm_applyOperatorToState_reindexState,
   110	    reindexOp_eprCrossSwap_place_AB'']

   112	/-- An operator placed on `BB'` has, on the expanded state, the same norm as
   113	the same operator placed on `BA''`, by invariance under the crosswise EPR
   114	exchange. -/
   115	theorem norm_place_BB'_eq_norm_place_BA'' (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   116	    (O : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace .bob)) :
   117	    ‖applyOperatorToState (S.place .BB' O) S.psiHat‖ =
   118	      ‖applyOperatorToState (S.place .BA'' O) S.psiHat‖ := by
   119	  conv_lhs => rw [← reindexState_eprCrossSwap_psiHat S]
   120	  rw [WinImplications.norm_applyOperatorToState_reindexState,
   121	    reindexOp_eprCrossSwap_place_BB']

   123	/-- Transfer of a same-side state-dependent distance between the `AA'` and
   124	`AB''` placements. -/
   125	theorem opFamilyDistSq_place_AB''_eq_AA' {X α : Type*} [Fintype α]
   126	    (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (μ : Distribution X)
   127	    (A B : X → α → Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace .alice)) :
   128	    opFamilyDistSq μ (fun x a => S.place .AB'' (A x a))
   129	        (fun x a => S.place .AB'' (B x a)) S.psiHat =
   130	      opFamilyDistSq μ (fun x a => S.place .AA' (A x a))
   131	        (fun x a => S.place .AA' (B x a)) S.psiHat := by
   132	  unfold opFamilyDistSq
   133	  refine avgOver_congr _ _ _ fun x => Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
   134	  rw [← place_sub, ← place_sub, norm_place_AB''_eq_norm_place_AA']
   135	  all_goals rfl

   137	/-- Transfer of a same-side state-dependent distance between the `BA''` and
   138	`BB'` placements. -/
   139	theorem opFamilyDistSq_place_BB'_eq_BA'' {X α : Type*} [Fintype α]
   140	    (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (μ : Distribution X)
   141	    (A B : X → α → Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace .bob)) :
   142	    opFamilyDistSq μ (fun x a => S.place .BB' (A x a))
   143	        (fun x a => S.place .BB' (B x a)) S.psiHat =
   144	      opFamilyDistSq μ (fun x a => S.place .BA'' (A x a))
   145	        (fun x a => S.place .BA'' (B x a)) S.psiHat := by
   146	  unfold opFamilyDistSq
   147	  refine avgOver_congr _ _ _ fun x => Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
   148	  rw [← place_sub, ← place_sub, norm_place_BB'_eq_norm_place_BA'']
   149	  all_goals rfl

    41	/-- The `AA'` placement is the reindexed left factor of the
    42	`AA' | BA''(B'B'')` bipartition. -/
    43	theorem place_AA'_eq (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
    44	    (O : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace Placement.AA'.side)) :
    45	    S.place .AA' O =
    46	      reindexOp (aaBaBipartition P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
    47	        (heteroKron O
    48	          (1 : Op ((S.toStrategy.ιB × PauliRegister P) ×
    49	            (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)))) :=
    50	  (reindexOp_aaBaBipartition_left S O).symm
    51	
    52	/-- The `BA''` placement is the reindexed right factor of the
    53	`AA' | BA''(B'B'')` bipartition. -/
    54	theorem place_BA''_eq (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
    55	    (O : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace Placement.BA''.side)) :
    56	    S.place .BA'' O =
    57	      reindexOp (aaBaBipartition P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
    58	        (heteroKron (1 : Op (S.toStrategy.ιA × PauliRegister P))
    59	          (heteroKron O (1 : Op (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)))) :=
    60	  (reindexOp_aaBaBipartition_right S O).symm
    61	
    62	/-- The `AB''` placement is the reindexed left factor of the
    63	`AB'' | BB'(A'A'')` bipartition. -/
    64	theorem place_AB''_eq (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
    65	    (O : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace Placement.AB''.side)) :
    66	    S.place .AB'' O =
    67	      reindexOp (abBbBipartition P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
    68	        (heteroKron O
    69	          (1 : Op ((S.toStrategy.ιB × PauliRegister P) ×
    70	            (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)))) :=
    71	  (reindexOp_abBbBipartition_left S O).symm
    72	
    73	/-- The `BB'` placement is the reindexed right factor of the
    74	`AB'' | BB'(A'A'')` bipartition. -/
    75	theorem place_BB'_eq (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
    76	    (O : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace Placement.BB'.side)) :
    77	    S.place .BB' O =
    78	      reindexOp (abBbBipartition P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)

    83	/-- Reindexing an operator commutes with the conjugate transpose. -/
    84	theorem reindexOp_conjTranspose {ι κ : Type*} (e : ι ≃ κ) (M : Op κ) :

    89	/-- Reindexing an operator along an equivalence preserves positivity. -/
    90	theorem reindexOp_nonneg {ι κ : Type*} [Finite ι] [Finite κ]
    91	    (e : ι ≃ κ) {M : Op κ} (hM : 0 ≤ M) :
    92	    0 ≤ reindexOp e M := by
    93	  letI := Fintype.ofFinite ι
    94	  letI := Fintype.ofFinite κ
    95	  rw [Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef] at hM ⊢

   101	/-- A placement is multiplicative. -/
   102	theorem place_mul (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) :
   103	    ∀ (p : Placement) (A B : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side)),
   104	      S.place p (A * B) = S.place p A * S.place p B

   108	        ← WinImplications.reindexOp_mul, heteroKron_mul, mul_one]
   109	      all_goals rfl
   110	  | .BA'', A, B => by
   111	      classical
   112	      rw [place_BA''_eq, place_BA''_eq, place_BA''_eq,
   113	        ← WinImplications.reindexOp_mul, heteroKron_mul, heteroKron_mul,
   114	        mul_one, mul_one]
   115	      all_goals rfl
   116	  | .BB', A, B => by
   117	      classical
   118	      rw [place_BB'_eq, place_BB'_eq, place_BB'_eq,
   119	        ← WinImplications.reindexOp_mul, heteroKron_mul, heteroKron_mul,
   120	        mul_one, mul_one]
   121	      all_goals rfl

   128	/-- A placement sends the local identity to the identity of the six-register
   129	space. -/
   130	theorem place_one (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (p : Placement) :

   132	  ext i j
   133	  cases p <;>
   134	    · simp only [ProjectiveSetting.place, Matrix.one_apply, Prod.ext_iff]
   135	      split_ifs <;> simp_all

   137	/-- A placement is additive over finite sums of local operators.
   138	Compatibility name for `place_finset_sum`, retained for the combining-point
   139	proofs that use this spelling. -/
   140	theorem place_finsetSum (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (p : Placement) {γ : Type*}
   141	    (s : Finset γ) (O : γ → Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side)) :
   142	    S.place p (∑ x ∈ s, O x) = ∑ x ∈ s, S.place p (O x) :=

   145	/-- A placement commutes with the conjugate transpose. -/
   146	theorem place_conjTranspose (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) :

   148	      S.place p Aᴴ = (S.place p A)ᴴ

   162	        WinImplications.heteroKron_conjTranspose, Matrix.conjTranspose_one,

   171	/-- A placement preserves positivity. -/
   172	theorem place_nonneg (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) :
   173	    ∀ (p : Placement) {A : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side)}, 0 ≤ A →
   174	      0 ≤ S.place p A

   198	/-- The placement of a local operator bounded by the identity is bounded by
   199	the identity. -/
   200	theorem place_le_one (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (p : Placement)
   201	    {A : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side)} (hA : A ≤ 1) :

+# Issue 515: Combined Line Measurement Consistency
+
+## Statement Integrity
+
+The source is `lem:qld-xz-lines`, especially
+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:900-961`.
+The blueprint entries are `lem:qld-xz-lines` and
+`lem:combined-line-measurement-consistency`.
+
+The paper starts with a normalized projective strategy passing with error
+`epsilon` and the previously constructed joint projective point measurements.
+Their self-consistency and both ordered-product comparisons hold with
+polynomially small point error. It concludes evaluated consistency of the
+explicit X-Z-X line POVM on two independent line-point samples, in every
+opposite placement, with polynomial error in `epsilon` and `md/q`.
+
+The internal Lean theorem first fixes `deltaQ` and `IsPolyErr deltaQ`, then
+chooses `deltaP`. It quantifies over admissible parameters, a projective
+setting, a `CombinedPointsWitness S (deltaQ epsilon)`, and every directed
+opposite placement. Its conclusion concerns `S.combinedLineMeasurement`
+itself under the original product distribution. The target header is
+byte-for-byte unchanged from `ae124f8f09ee002444ac5b9711822c0f1daae142`.
+
+Verdict: exact preservation of the existing internal theorem. The source
+existence theorem still obtains its point witness internally. No new
+hypothesis, altered quantifier, weakened conclusion, changed measurement,
+or error convention is introduced. The existing additive interpretation of
+two-variable polynomial error is retained.
+
+## Mathematical Proof
+
+The two completed point-to-line marginal defects are at most
+`Delta = 8 * deltaQ(epsilon) + C * (epsilon + sqrt(epsilon))`.
+Conditioning on a nonzero X-line direction retains mass `r >= 1/2` and
+increases these bounds to `Delta/r`. Uniform affine resampling and the
+coefficient-polynomial root bound give the conditional collision estimate
+`md/q`. These facts are proved, not assumed.
+
+The existing heterogeneous pasting theorem needs only the two marginal
+comparisons. Reindexing each directed opposite placement preserves the state
+norm and all consistency expressions; the unused registers stay on the
+line side. Ordering answers Z then X makes its output exactly the X-Z-X
+sandwich. Reversing the answer order preserves the defect.
+
+The measurement does not change on conditioning. The discarded mass is at
+most `1/(2q)`, and every pointwise defect is at most one. Restoration gives
+`r * pastingError(md/q, Delta/r) + 1/(2q)`. The independent unit bound and
+the existing `exists_conditioned_polynomial_bound` produce `deltaP`.

blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:202:	The source states the two line-versus-point clauses with ``the'' $t \in \F_q$ such that $x_{\overline w} = u_0 + t v$. When the direction is nonzero and $x_{\overline w}$ lies on the line, exactly one such $t$ exists and the formulation above agrees with the source. But zero directions occur: Definition~\ref{def:line} explicitly permits them, and the question distribution of Definition~\ref{def:ld-question-distribution} produces $\mathsf{DLine}$ questions with $v' = \pi_{i-1}(v) = 0$ with positive probability, namely whenever the last $m - i + 1$ coordinates of $v$ vanish. In that case $\ell(u_0, 0) = \{u_0\}$, every $t \in \F_q$ satisfies $x_{\overline w} = u_0 + t v'$ when $x_{\overline w} = u_0$, and the source clause does not determine acceptance for a nonconstant answer polynomial. The universal quantification over $t$ adopted in Definition~\ref{def:ld-win-predicate} makes the predicate a well-defined function of its arguments; it accepts vacuously when no such $t$ exists, a case the question distribution never produces. Completeness is unaffected: the restriction of a polynomial $g$ to the singleton line $\ell(u_0,0)$, expressed through the parameterization $t \mapsto u_0 + t \cdot 0$, is the constant polynomial with value $g(u_0)$, which passes the check for every $t$. Soundness is likewise unaffected: zero directions occur with probability at most $2/(mq)$, so any acceptance convention on this event changes success probabilities by at most that amount; the game-correspondence obligation enumerated in the proof of Theorem~\ref{lem:ld-soundness} accounts for this event explicitly, and an error of this shape is absorbed into the universal constants of $\delta_{\mathrm{ld}}$.

blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:272:		\item (\emph{Game correspondence.}) The source asserts that the two games are identical; they are not. In the cited test, the subcube commutation and pair-synchronicity branches send an ordered pair of points of a \emph{hidden} subcube and receive a pair of field values --- a question type that $\mathfrak{G}^{\mathrm{ld}}$ does not have --- its line questions carry no analogue of the seed $s$, its nontrivial cross-tests have mass $1/3$ where the present ones have $2/9$, and it fixes no acceptance convention on the zero-direction event of Remark~\ref{rem:ld-win-zero-direction}, whose probability is at most $\frac1m \sum_{j=1}^m q^{-j} \le \frac{1}{m(q-1)} \le \frac{2}{mq}$ over uniform $(s,v)$. What must be proved is a reduction converting any projective strategy for $\mathfrak{G}^{\mathrm{ld}}$ with success probability $1-\eps$ into a two-prover strategy for the tensor-code test with rejection probability at most $\tfrac32\,\eps + O(1/(mq))$ --- the factor $\tfrac32$ being the target bookkeeping constant from the branch weights, and the $O(1/(mq))$ the zero-direction term. A deficit of this shape is then absorbed into $\delta_{\mathrm{ld}}$ by enlarging the universal constant $a$, since $(x+y)^b \le x^b + y^b$ for $0 < b \le 1$ and $(2/(mq))^b \le 2\,q^{-b}$ for $m \ge 1$, using $dmk \ge 1$.

\section{At a glance}

\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Difficulty: easy.}  No step of the retained proof route is
  in doubt.  The obstruction is that the error function claimed in the
  statement of the combined-lines lemma of the Pauli basis analysis,
  $\poly(m^2\eps, md/q)$, is not delivered by either of the two
  derivations printed in its source proof: one route establishes
  $m \cdot \poly(\eps, md/q)$, the other would give
  $m^2 \cdot \poly(\eps, md/q)$ and rests in addition on a distributional
  decomposition that the stated sub-line lemma does not supply.  The
  correction is to state the first route's established error form and confirm
  that the sole consumer tolerates it.
  The unrestricted supplied-point domain of the current extended-line helper
  has a separate obstruction: deterministic quadratic point answers force a
  positive axis-line error even on a perfect strategy. This does not refute
  the paper statement, which uses its previously constructed point family.
  \item \textbf{Key Mathlib inputs:} the
  Cauchy--Schwarz inequality for state-dependent operator distances
  (project-local, blueprint Chapter 12), mixture decompositions of
  question distributions, and elementary averaging over restricted
  line distributions; no new Mathlib surface beyond finite
  expectations and inner-product estimates already used by the
  low individual degree development.
  \item \textbf{Estimated weight:} a \textbf{statement-level error-form
  decision} plus about \textbf{one lemma interface} of checking that the
  consumer absorbs an $m$ prefactor into its constants; the three chained
  claims behind the retained route are ordinary Cauchy--Schwarz estimates,
  on the order of \textbf{a few hundred lines} of formal proof in total
  when that part of the development is reached.
  \item \textbf{Mathlib/project split:} essentially \textbf{100\%
  project-local}.  The estimates use only the project's state-dependent
  distance calculus, the sub-line distribution, and elementary
  probability on finite sets.
  \item \textbf{Key inputs:} the combined point and line measurements and
  the sub-line distribution of the Pauli basis analysis in
  \cite{Ji2020MIPStar}, and the error function of the classical soundness
  theorem imported from \cite{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree}, into which the
  corrected error form must be absorbed.  The blueprint correction is tracked
  in \ghissue{173}.
\end{itemize}

\section{Key theorem forms}

Throughout, $(q,m,d)$ is an admissible parameter tuple of the Pauli basis
test, $\ket{\hat\psi}$ is the expanded state of the projective strategy
under analysis, succeeding with probability at least $1-\eps$, and all
approximations are with respect to $\ket{\hat\psi}$.  For lines
$\ell_X, \ell_Z$ in $\F_q^m$, the POVM $\{T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}\}$,
with outcomes pairs of polynomials of degree at most $md$ on the two
lines, is the two-basis combined line measurement, and
$\{\hat Q^{x,z}_{a,b}\}$ is the combined point measurement; their
consistency errors are $\delta_P = \poly(\eps, md/q)$ and
$\delta_Q = \poly(\eps)$ respectively, and
$\delta_{\mathrm{Line}} = \poly(\eps)$ is the line--point consistency
error of the strategy.  The lemma under discussion asserts that a
measurement $\{\hat Q^{\ell}_f\}$, built for each line $\ell$ in
$\F_q^{2m+2}$, is $\delta_{\mathrm{combine}}$-consistent, on average over
the line-point distribution over $\F_q^{2m+2}$, with the combined point
measurement on the extended coordinates, together with the
register-swapped counterpart.%
\footnote{In the mirror of the source consulted here,
\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex}: the
lemma statement, with the error form $\poly(m^2\eps, md/q)$, is at
lines~1020--1034 (label \path{lem:qld-4-13}); the central display with
the first-route bound at lines~1134--1137
(label \path{eq:qld-combined-lines-consistency}); the three claims at
lines~1140--1239 (labels \path{claim:17-1}--\path{claim:17-3}); the
second-route conclusion $O(m^2\delta_P)$ at lines~1241--1245, preceded by
a duplicated sentence whose second copy carries a malformed reference;
the product-distribution estimate invoked there at lines~1055--1061
(label \path{eq:qld-xz-lines-restricted}); and the sub-line lemma at
lines~1063--1116 (label \path{lem:qld-sublines}).}
The comparison involves four forms of the error function
$\delta_{\mathrm{combine}}(\eps,m,d,q)$.
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \textbf{Source form.}
  $\delta_{\mathrm{combine}} = \poly(m^2\eps,\, md/q)$.  This is the form
  printed in the statement.  Neither printed derivation supports it.
  \item \textbf{Established form (first route).}
  $\delta_{\mathrm{combine}}
  = O\big(m\,(\eps^{1/4} + \delta_P^{1/4} + \delta_Q^{1/4}
  + \delta_{\mathrm{Line}}^{1/2})\big)$, a function of the form
  $m \cdot \poly(\eps,\, md/q)$.
  \item \textbf{Second-route form (conditional).}
  $\delta_{\mathrm{combine}} = O(m^2 \delta_P)
  = m^2 \cdot \poly(\eps,\, md/q)$, conditional on a joint-law
  decomposition that the sub-line lemma, as stated, does not provide.
  \item \textbf{Consumer requirement.}  The unique consumer, the
  polynomial-pair lemma, feeds $\delta_{\mathrm{combine}}$ into an error
  of the form
  $a(md)^a(\delta_{\mathrm{combine}}^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$ imported
  from \cite{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree}; any bound
  $m^{O(1)} \cdot \poly(\eps, md/q)$ is absorbed by enlarging $a$ and
  shrinking $b$, so forms~2 and~3 both suffice downstream.
\end{enumerate}

\section{The domain of the conditional Lean helper}

The source statement does not take an arbitrary joint point measurement as an
input.  It uses the family $\{\hat Q^{x,z}_{a,b}\}$ constructed by the preceding
point lemma, whose error has the form $\delta_Q(\eps)=\poly(\eps)$.  Consequently,
an internal theorem which accepts an already constructed point witness must retain
the same quantitative dependency: it should first fix a function
$\delta_Q:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ satisfying the one-variable polynomial-error
predicate, then choose $\delta_P$, and at strategy error $\eps$ accept only a
point witness with bound $\delta_Q(\eps)$.

Before the repair tracked by \ghissue{389}, the Lean helper
\path{exists_combinedLinesWitness_ofPointsWitness} instead had the quantifier
order
\[
  \exists\delta_P=\poly(\eps,md/q)\quad
  \forall\eps\ \forall\delta_Q\ \forall Q,
  \qquad Q\text{ has point error at most }\delta_Q
  \Longrightarrow T\text{ has line error at most }\delta_P(\eps,md/q).
\]
Thus the line-error function was chosen before an unrestricted scalar
$\delta_Q$, and did not depend on it.  The fields of
\path{CombinedPointsWitness} bound self-consistency and the two ordered-product
comparisons by precisely this scalar; they impose no relation between an
arbitrary $\delta_Q$ and $\eps$.  The conditioned-pasting estimate therefore
cannot eliminate $\delta_Q$ from its conclusion.

There is a concrete mathematical obstruction to the old domain.  Set
$\eps=0$, take $m=1$ and fixed $d$, and let $q$ grow through admissible field
sizes with $q>d+1$.  On any perfect strategy, define the supplied projective
joint point measurement deterministically, with X answer $x^{d+1}$ and a fixed
Z answer, identically on the two player sides.  Its self-consistency defect is
zero, while the two ordered-product defects are finite and hence can be covered
by a sufficiently large scalar $\delta_Q$, which the old helper quantified
arbitrarily.  On an axis X line, however, every outcome allowed by
\path{CombinedLinesWitness.axis_degree_X} evaluates as a polynomial of degree at
most $d$.  Its difference from $x^{d+1}$ has at most $d+1$ roots, so even after
mixing line outcomes the disagreement probability on that line is at least
$1-(d+1)/q$.  Since axis lines have fixed positive weight in the line-point
law, the resulting line consistency defect stays bounded away from zero as
$q\to\infty$.  In contrast, the two-variable polynomial-error predicate forces
$\delta_P(0,d/q)\to0$.  This argument diagnoses the theorem interface; no Lean
counterexample theorem is asserted here.

The repaired conditional helper has the form
\[
  \forall\delta_Q,\quad \delta_Q=\poly(\eps)\Longrightarrow
  \exists\delta_P=\poly(\eps,md/q)\quad
  \forall\eps\ \forall Q\text{ with error }\delta_Q(\eps),\quad
  \exists T\text{ with error }\delta_P(\eps,md/q).
\]
This is not a new hypothesis on the paper theorem.  The source-facing Lean
declaration \path{exists_combinedLinesWitness} preserves its original statement:
it existentially obtains $\delta_Q$ and its point witnesses from the preceding
point construction, then applies the conditional helper.

The construction is proved in
\path{combined_line_measurement_consistency}. For a joint point family
with error $\delta_Q(\eps)=\poly(\eps)$, it establishes evaluated consistency
of the explicit unconditioned measurement
\[
 T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}
 =L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X)L^Z_{f_Z}(\ell_Z)L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X)
\]
under the original product of line-point distributions, with error
$\delta_P(\eps,md/q)=\poly(\eps,md/q)$ and every directed opposite
placement. The point-to-line comparisons at source lines 900--941 and the
pasting argument at lines 942--961 give the proof. The POVM,
axis-degree properties, and X marginal of this same measurement are proved.

The proof conditions the question distribution on nonzero X-line direction;
the measurement itself remains the displayed sandwich. Write $r$ for the
retained mass. Every axis line has nonzero direction, so $r\ge1/2$.
The completed point-to-line marginal defects are bounded by
$\Delta=8\delta_Q(\eps)+C(\eps+\sqrt{\eps})$ before conditioning and by
$\Delta/r$ afterwards, for a universal $C\ge1$. Uniform affine-parameter
resampling and the univariate root bound give the conditional collision
parameter $md/q$.

The heterogeneous pasting theorem, with the answers ordered Z then X,
therefore bounds the conditional defect of this same sandwich by
$\delta_{\mathrm{pasting}}(md/q,\Delta/r)$. On the discarded event the
pointwise defect is at most one. Its probability is at most $1/(2q)$:
axis lines contribute zero, and the last raw direction coordinate of a
diagonal line is uniform. Consequently the defect under the original law
is at most
\[
 r\,\delta_{\mathrm{pasting}}(md/q,\Delta/r)+\frac1{2q}.
\]
Taking the minimum with the independent unit bound and using
$1/2\le r\le1$ and $md\ge1$ gives a polynomial error in the corrected sum
sense. This proves the original unconditioned statement without an
additional hypothesis.\footnote{Recovered and checked under \ghissue{515}.
The conditional and restored estimates are
\path{exists_combinedLine_conditioned_defect_le} and
\path{exists_combinedLine_restored_defect_le}; the final scalar step is
\path{exists_conditioned_polynomial_bound}.}

\subsection{The extended-line supplied-point obstruction}

The same quantitative omission remains in the auxiliary
\path{exists_extendedLinesWitness_ofPointsWitness}: a single polynomial error
function is chosen before an arbitrary scalar $\delta_Q$ and every point witness
at that error. Passing from paired points to the extended scalar answer does
not remove this obstruction. The first-route estimate
$C m g(\eps,md/q)$ in
\path{exists_extendedLinesWitness_established_ofPointsWitness} has the same
problem: it still tends to zero at $\eps=0$ with fixed $m,d$ and increasing $q$.
These unrestricted auxiliaries are tracked by \ghissue{509} and \ghissue{511},
respectively. The source instead uses the family constructed by its point lemma,
with $\delta_Q=\poly(\eps)$, and defines the scalar answer by
$c=\alpha a+\beta b$. Claim~17-1 explicitly retains the point error.
\footnote{The source passages are \path{lem:qld-4-10}, \path{lem:qld-4-12}, and
\path{claim:17-1} in
\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex},
lines~689--709, 993--1018, and 1140--1173.}

Take $m=d=1$, $\eps=0$, and let $q=2^{2k+1}>2$ tend to infinity.
These parameters are admissible. The Pauli basis test has a perfect projective strategy by
\path{lem:pauli-completeness}.\footnote{See
\path{references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex},
lines~1229--1421, for the construction; the statement and its projective Pauli
measurements appear at lines~1232--1255.}
Let $\hat\psi$ be its normalized expanded state. On each player's expanded
local space, define the supplied joint point measurement by
\[
 Q^{x,z}_{a,b}=
 \begin{cases}
   \Id,&(a,b)=(x^2,0),\\
   0,&\text{otherwise}.
 \end{cases}
\]
This is a complete projective measurement and is exactly self-consistent in
every opposite placement. The finitely many averaged squared distances from the
two ordered expanded point products are finite real numbers. Taking their
maximum and zero gives a scalar $\delta_Q$ satisfying all the fields of the
point witness. No estimate of this scalar in terms of $\eps$ is required.

The extended point answer is $\alpha x^2$. In dimension $2m+2=4$, the directly
indexed line-point law assigns weight $1/2$ to axis lines and then chooses one
of the four coordinates uniformly. Its X-axis branch therefore has mass $1/8$.
On that branch, $z,\alpha,\beta$ are fixed along the line, while $x$ is uniform
in the field. The canonical base has X coordinate zero, so the affine line
parameter is exactly $x$. For $\alpha\ne0$, every permitted line answer $p$
has degree at most one, and $p(X)-\alpha X^2$ is a nonzero polynomial of degree
two. It has at most two roots, hence its agreement with the point answer is at
most $2/q$.

This bound also holds for any line POVM. Indeed, for a fixed line let $w_p$
be the expectation of its effect for $p$ in the expanded state, at the line
player's placement. Positivity and completeness give $w_p\ge0$ and
$\sum_p w_p=1$; the axis-degree field makes $w_p=0$ for higher-degree answers.
The opposite point effect is deterministically the identity at $\alpha x^2$,
so the agreement is precisely the $w_p$-weighted average of those root-count
fractions. These weights depend on the line but not on $x$ along it. Averaging
over the fixed coordinates, and using nonnegativity of the defect on the
remaining question branches, gives for either player orientation
\[
 \operatorname{defect}\ \ge\
 \frac18\left(1-\frac1q\right)\left(1-\frac2q\right).
\]

\section{At a glance}

\textbf{Difficulty.} The domain correction is elementary; the remaining
formal estimate requires the project's state-dependent Cauchy--Schwarz and
restricted-distribution arguments. \textbf{Estimated weight.} The correction
affects two Lean modules and their blueprint correspondence. It retains the
unfinished scalar estimate and isolates the existing pasting consistency
obligation. \textbf{Mathlib/project split.} Finite sums, positivity, and real
square roots use Mathlib; the measurement construction and subline law use
the local quantum API. \textbf{Key mathematical inputs.} Completeness of a
POVM, projectivity, and Cauchy--Schwarz suffice for the counterexample and
the proposed source proof. The counterexample below is a mathematical
calculation, not a kernel-certified Lean instance.

\section{Key theorem forms}

Let $\widehat\psi$ be the normalized expanded state of a projective strategy
winning the Pauli basis test with probability at least $1-\eps$. Write
$L^W_f(\ell)$ and $M^W_a(u)$ for its expanded line and point effects. For
the subline law $D$, abbreviate the two correlations by
\begin{align*}
 A(T)&=\E_D\E_{(x,z,\alpha,\beta)\in\ell}
   \sum_{f_X,f_Z}\langle\widehat\psi,
   (T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}\ot
     M^Z_{f_Z(z)}(z)M^X_{f_X(x)}(x))\widehat\psi\rangle,\\
 B(T)&=\E_D\E_{(x,z,\alpha,\beta)\in\ell}
   \sum_{f_X,f_Z}\langle\widehat\psi,
   (T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}\ot
     M^Z_{f_Z(z)}(z))\widehat\psi\rangle.
\end{align*}
The paper's Claim 17-2 states
\[
 |A(T)-B(T)|\leq O\bigl(m\sqrt{\delta_{\mathrm{Line}}(\eps)}\bigr)
 \quad\text{for}\quad
 T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}
 =L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X)L^Z_{f_Z}(\ell_Z)L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X).
\]
The former Lean declaration quantified instead over every paired-line POVM
with the degree support and evaluated consistency conclusions of the
combined-lines lemma. Its scalar errors $\delta_P,\delta_Q$ were arbitrary,
independently of $\eps$. The right-hand side remained the same, with
$\delta_{\mathrm{Line}}(\eps)=\sqrt\eps$.

\section{The construction used by the source}

The paired-line measurement is defined by the displayed sandwich in the
proof of the combined-lines lemma. Claim 17-2 uses this definition to sum
over the Z polynomial:
\[
 \sum_{f_Z}T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}
 =L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X)
   \Bigl(\sum_{f_Z}L^Z_{f_Z}(\ell_Z)\Bigr)L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X)
 =L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X).
\]
The last equality uses completeness and projectivity. Cauchy--Schwarz
reduces the scalar difference to the square root of the resulting
X-line/point consistency deficit. The separate X marginal of the subline
law is sufficient; no joint conditional law for $(x,z)$ is needed.
Restriction to a line kind and coordinate costs a factor $2m$, so the
resulting square-root estimate is bounded by the paper's stated error
because $m\geq1$.\footnote{The construction is at lines 942--949 and the
claim and calculation at lines 1168--1201 of
\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex},
labels \path{lem:qld-xz-lines} and \path{claim:17-2} in
\cite{Ji2020MIPStar}. The repair is tracked by \ghissue{414}; the earlier
proof attempt is \ghissue{405}.}

\section{A counterexample to the enlarged domain}

Choose an admissible tuple with $q>1$ and a perfect projective strategy.
The honest strategy in the completeness lemma supplies one; for example,
$(q,m,d)=(8,1,1)$ is admissible. Its expanded state has norm one. For
$a\in\F_q$, let $c_a$ be the constant polynomial with value $a$. For both
players and every line pair, define a POVM by
\[
 T_{c_a,c_b}=q^{-2}I\quad(a,b\in\F_q),\qquad
 T_{f_X,f_Z}=0\quad\text{for every other pair}.
\]
There are $q^2$ nonzero effects, so they sum to $I$. Both axis-degree
requirements hold. At any incident point a constant polynomial has a
uniquely determined value, even on a zero-direction line. Thus the optional
evaluation in Lean returns the ordinary field value, never an undefined
outcome, for every nonzero effect in this example.

The evaluated POVM is uniform on the $q^2$ point pairs. Against any complete
joint point measurement $Q$, its agreement is $q^{-2}$ and its consistency
defect is $1-q^{-2}$. Therefore the line-witness requirements hold with
$\delta_P=1$ in every opposite placement. A point witness also exists within
the former public domain: take the projective measurement which always
answers $(0,0)$. It is exactly self-consistent and has both ordered-product
distances at most $4$. Indeed, the squared norms of either ordered product
family sum to one, by projectivity and completeness, and
\begin{align*}
 \sum_{a,b}\|(Q_{a,b}-M^X_aM^Z_b)\widehat\psi\|^2
 &\leq 2\sum_{a,b}\|Q_{a,b}\widehat\psi\|^2\\
 &\quad+2\sum_{a,b}\|M^X_aM^Z_b\widehat\psi\|^2\\
 &=4.
\end{align*}
The reversed ordering satisfies the same calculation. Hence $\delta_Q=4$
is allowed by every point-witness field. These constants are permitted by
the former scalar quantifiers; the argument does not require them to be
polynomially small functions of $\eps$.

For each supported subline sample, completeness gives
\[
 A(T)=q^{-2}\sum_{a,b}\langle\widehat\psi,
    (I\ot M^Z_bM^X_a)\widehat\psi\rangle=q^{-2},
 \qquad
 B(T)=q^{-2}\sum_{a,b}\langle\widehat\psi,
    (I\ot M^Z_b)\widehat\psi\rangle=q^{-1}.
\]
The first equality uses $\sum_bM^Z_b\sum_aM^X_a=I$, without a commutation
assumption. Probability averaging preserves these constants. The absolute
difference is therefore $(q-1)/q^2>0$, whereas the claimed bound is zero at
$\eps=0$. For $q=8$ the difference is $7/64$. The same perfect strategy is
admissible at arbitrarily small positive $\eps$, so excluding zero or
enlarging a universal constant cannot repair the claim. No polynomially
vanishing error depending on $\eps$ alone absorbs this difference.

\section{Blueprint and formal comparison}

The concrete measurement domain is retained. The scalar obligation now
compares complex expectations with the complex modulus, preserving the
universal constant, factor $m$, and square-root error. It is named
\leanid{subline\_remove\_X\_factor\_direct}. Its distribution is still the
directly indexed law represented by \leanid{SubLineWitness}, not the
source law $D$. Thus it is a formalization-only obligation, linked from
\path{lem:claim-17-2-direct}, and is not a formalization of the source
claim. The source statement remains at \path{lem:claim-17-2}, with neither
a Lean link nor a completion mark.

The same scalar distinction affects Claim 17-1: an ordered product
$M^Z_bM^X_a$ need not be Hermitian, so a bound on the real part of its
correlation does not bound its complex modulus. The proved real-part
estimate is retained as
\leanid{subline\_replace\_by\_ordered\_product\_re\_direct}.
Its constant is $2\sqrt{\delta_Q}$: the squared-distance comparison on
one placement is $4\delta_Q$ and uses $W^\dagger W$, not $W^2$.
The source Claim 17-1 remains a separate uncertified blueprint statement.
Likewise \leanid{subline\_Z\_term\_near\_one\_re\_direct} retains the
proved real Z-overlap estimate with its directly indexed domain explicit.
No reality or distribution-transport theorem is asserted by these renamings.
The three existing source blueprint statements are reused; no duplicate
source theorem with a new proof hole is introduced.

The distribution discrepancy is documented in
\path{docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex}. Admissibility
does not supply the divisibility needed to instantiate the source line law
at dimension $2m+2$. The current correction neither adds that divisibility
as a hypothesis nor identifies the directly indexed law with the source law.
Scalar realignment is tracked in \ghissue{474} and review of PR~478.
The distribution and complex-overlap work under \ghissue{118} remains open;
its historical budget is unchanged.

The abstract combined-line witness record remains unchanged. Its fields
faithfully express the existential conclusion of the combined-lines lemma,
but do not characterize the construction used in its proof. The internal
consistency theorem refers to the concrete sandwich. Both witness
existence proofs construct their records with that measurement. A later
argument needing the exact construction can use the consistency theorem
and the same explicit record; merely choosing an unspecified existential
witness does not recover its defining formula.\footnote{The Lean-only
theorem is \leanid{combined\_line\_measurement\_consistency} in
\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines.lean}. Its hypotheses explicitly supply
a polynomially controlled point family. Issue \#515 proves it by the
source's point-to-line comparisons and pasting argument, with the
original distribution restored after conditioning. The source-facing
\leanid{exists\_combinedLinesWitness} has an unchanged statement.}

The remaining direct proof hole in the affected modules is
\leanid{subline\_remove\_X\_factor\_direct}: apply complex
weighted Cauchy--Schwarz to bound $|A(T)-B(T)|$ by the square root of the
X-overlap deficit, then use the already proved
\leanid{exists\_concreteXPointOverlap\_deficit\_le}. That estimate already
uses \leanid{combinedLineMeasurement\_sum\_Z}, expanded line-point
consistency, and the separate X marginal of the directly indexed law.
Transport of this argument and of the real-part estimates to the source
law, including the complex estimate of Claim 17-1, is a separate remaining
obligation. No additional hole is introduced for that transport.

The theorem \leanid{combined\_line\_measurement\_consistency}
proves consistency of the same unconditioned X-Z-X measurement
with the supplied polynomially controlled joint point family on the
original product of line-point distributions, in every opposite placement.
The source point-to-line comparison, conditioned pasting estimate, and
restoration of the discarded contribution are described in
\path{docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_combined-lines-error-term.tex}.
No marginal identity, deficit bound, or producer is added to a paper theorem.

\section{Conclusion}

The discrepancy lies in the formal quantification over arbitrary witnesses,
not in the paper's constructed-measurement assertion. The counterexample
forces a domain correction. Using the defined sandwich restores the measurement domain. The complex
scalar conclusion is restored for the directly indexed auxiliary obligation;
transport to the source distribution remains open. The combined-line
consistency construction is proved. The source claims retain their complex-modulus statements
without unsupported formalization marks.

\section{Conclusion}

There is a proof-level gap in the cited lemma, together with an
intermediate inconsistency: the printed proof asserts two different
bounds for the same consistency defect, the first-route bound
$O(m(\eps^{1/4} + \delta_P^{1/4} + \delta_Q^{1/4} +
\delta_{\mathrm{Line}}^{1/2}))$ and the second-route bound
$O(m^2\delta_P)$, the second resting on a joint-law decomposition that
the sub-line lemma as stated does not supply; and the error form claimed
in the lemma statement, $\poly(m^2\eps, md/q)$, follows from neither.
The first route is sound after a harmless deficit correction in its
second claim and establishes $m \cdot \poly(\eps, md/q)$.  The
discrepancy is harmless downstream, since the sole consumer absorbs
polynomial-in-$m$ prefactors into its constants.  The blueprint therefore
retains the printed statement with the missing step explicitly tracked, uses
the corrected first-route form in the proof and in the sequel, and cites this
note; strengthening the sub-line lemma to license the second route is
optional, and no route to the printed form is currently known.  We do not
assert that the printed form is false.

The measurements of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-12} and Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-13}
constitute a strategy for the classical low individual degree game in $2m+2$
	by a base point $u_0$ and a direction $v$ --- for the lines arising as
	question contents, the pair read off the line's description, whose base
	point is the canonical representative of
	Definition~\ref{def:line-representative} --- and an integer $c \geq 0$,
	we write $\deg_c(\ell)$ for the set of univariate polynomials of degree
	at most $c$, each given by its list of $c+1$ coefficients and identified
	by its polynomial representative rather than by the function it induces,
	as in Definition~\ref{def:polyfunc}; the argument $\ell$ records the
	line to which such an answer refers, through the parameterization
	$t \mapsto u_0 + tv$. The cases used below are $\deg_d(\ell)$ and
	$\deg_{md}(\ell)$; whenever $d \leq md$, extending coefficient lists by
	zeros gives the inclusion $\deg_d(\ell) \subseteq \deg_{md}(\ell)$. For
	$f \in \deg_c(\ell)$, $u \in \ell$, and $a \in \F_q$, we say that $f$
	\emph{evaluates to $a$ at $u$}, written $f(u) = a$, if $f(t) = a$ for
	every $t \in \F_q$ with $u = u_0 + tv$. When $v \neq 0$ this $t$ is
	unique, so every $f$ evaluates at every point of $\ell$; when $v = 0$,
	so that $\ell = \{u_0\}$, exactly those $f$ that induce a constant
	function on $\F_q$ evaluate at $u_0$, to their constant value. An
	operator indexed by $f(u)$ is understood to be the zero operator when
	$f$ does not evaluate at $u$, and for a family $\{N_f\}$ indexed by
	$f \in \deg_c(\ell)$ we write
	$N_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot)=a]} = \sum_{f \colon f(u) = a} N_f$; when
	$v = 0$ the classes indexed by $a \in \F_q$ form a sub-measurement
	rather than a partition of the outcomes. The \emph{completed} family of
	evaluation classes is the family indexed by $a \in \F_q \cup \{\bot\}$
	obtained by adjoining the additional class
	$N_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot)=\bot]} = \sum_{f} N_f$, the sum over those
	$f$ that do not evaluate at $u$; when $\{N_f\}$ is a POVM,
	respectively a projective measurement, the completed classes form one
	as well, and when $v \neq 0$ the class
	$N_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot)=\bot]}$ is the zero operator.
\end{definition}

\begin{remark}[Line answers as coefficient lists]
	\label{rem:deg-line-representatives}
	The source refers to the elements of $\deg_{md}(\ell)$ as polynomials
	``defined on the line $\ell$'', that is, as functions on the point set
	of $\ell$, while its decision procedure expects each line answer as a
	list of coefficients. The two readings differ. When $md \geq q$,
	distinct coefficient lists induce the same function $\F_q \to \F_q$;
	and when $\ell$ has direction $v = 0$ --- a case the question
	distributions produce with positive probability
	(Remark~\ref{rem:ld-win-zero-direction}) --- the point set of $\ell$ is
	the singleton $\{u_0\}$, so a function on $\ell$ retains only a single
	field element of the answer. Definition~\ref{def:ideg-deg-polynomials}
	therefore adopts the coefficient reading, under which the strategy's
	line measurements are indexed by exactly the answers of the prescribed
	form, and its evaluation convention reproduces the universal
	quantification of the line-versus-point clauses of the win predicates
	(Definition~\ref{def:ld-win-predicate}).
\end{remark}

    25	theorem avgOver_restrict_mul_mass {Sample : Type*} [DecidableEq Sample]
    26	    (dist : Distribution Sample) (good : Sample -> Prop) [DecidablePred good]
    27	    (hpos : 0 < ∑ sample ∈ dist.support.filter good, dist.weight sample)
    28	    (value : Sample -> ℝ) :
    29	    (∑ sample ∈ dist.support.filter good, dist.weight sample) *
    30	      avgOver (Distribution.restrict dist good hpos) value =
    31	      ∑ sample ∈ dist.support.filter good, dist.weight sample * value sample := by
    32	  unfold avgOver Distribution.restrict
    33	  rw [Finset.mul_sum]
    34	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    35	  intro sample hsample
    36	  simp only [if_pos (Finset.mem_filter.mp hsample).2]
    37	  field_simp

    40	the inverse retained mass. This is a formalization-only finite probability

    45	    (hpos : 0 < ∑ sample ∈ dist.support.filter good, dist.weight sample)
    46	    (value : Sample -> ℝ) (hnonneg : ∀ sample, 0 ≤ value sample) :
    47	    avgOver (Distribution.restrict dist good hpos) value ≤
